title: Acme Mobile
subtitle: iOS UX Audit
tagline: A screen-by-screen walkthrough of the app as it stands today, every route, every state, pre-annotated for markup.

meta.data: Synthetic throughout: the app's review fixture plus a local fixture server. No real user data appears anywhere.

caveat: Driven on a simulator, in a debug build, against fixture data. Finding B1.1 should be reproduced on a release build before it is treated as a shipping defect, and treated as one until that check is clean.

sections.title: Authentication and onboarding
sections.blurb: Cold launch to the first authenticated screen: sign-in, recovery, and the gate that stands between a new user and the app.

sections.title: Home
sections.blurb: The first tab: the balance, the banners, and what the app chooses to put in front of a user first.

notes.text: The primary action is dimmed until the email parses and a password exists. Nothing says why, so a mistyped address reads as a broken button.
"Forgot password?" is the only recovery route and sits below the fold once the keyboard opens.
Legal line and account creation are present and legible.

screens.title: Sign in, keyboard up
screens.where: Same screen with the software keyboard open

notes.text: The keyboard covers the recovery link entirely. A user who has forgotten their password has to dismiss the keyboard to find out that recovery exists.
False overdue banner. useGracePeriod unwraps with data?.data ?? data, so the documented { data: null } reply returns the truthy wrapper and a user in good standing sees "NaN days remaining".
This card calls the balance Reserve; the account tab calls the same figure Balance. Two names, one concept.
The balance is the clearest money moment in the app: one big figure with the contribution and the return in one glance.
"Next appointment" shows the provider and the visit type but no date or time.
